blocks.x: Data & Lakehouse applied to Warehousing & Fulfillment. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

Fulfillment is throughput economics: pick rates, dock scheduling, labor allocation and inventory truth. Orchestrated robots, vision-verified quality and agentic labor planning compound into cost-per-order leadership.

At Logistics & Supply Chain level this capability reads as: lane-level scope 3 transport emissions with methodology lineage (CSRD-grade reporting automated). The sub-industry page narrows it to the unit's workflows, regimes and KPIs.

Programs run on a fixed rhythm so progress is visible from week one. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
